- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer below forecast for volatility.
- When sentiment alternates between bullish/bearish (e.g., 0.33/1.00), model exhibits lagged response; align forecast with 2–3 day sentiment average, not raw history.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overfit recent supply shocks; dampen forecast sensitivity to auction events unless sentiment confirms bullishness.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 30d forecast mean, check sentiment history for 3-day rolling average — if sentiment is neutral or bearish, adjust forecast downward by 1–3%.
- For 30d forecasts with high volatility (e.g., >10% range in 10d), apply mean reversion: cap forecast at ±2.5% of 30d mean unless sentiment strongly bullish.
